title: Fix login approval gating with fresh Firestore server reads at users/{auth.uid}

requirements.summary: Force every login attempt to perform a fresh Firestore server read from users/{auth.uid} and gate login solely on that document’s approved boolean.
acceptanceCriteria: On each login attempt, the app fetches Firestore document users/{uid} where uid equals the authenticated Firebase user UID, using a server-forced read API (not a cache-eligible read).
If the Firestore document users/{uid} exists and approved === true (boolean), login succeeds and the pending-approval error is not shown.
If the Firestore document users/{uid} is missing OR approved !== true, the app signs the user out and shows the exact message: "Your account is pending admin approval."
Toggling approved: false → true in Firestore and attempting login again (without hard refresh) reflects the new approval state, proving there is no cached approval result.

file_operations.description: Update the login-time approval check to always read only the exact Firestore document users/{auth.uid} using a server-forced read function (e.g., Firestore server read helper rather than cache-eligible reads). Ensure the approved field is treated as the sole source of truth and must be exactly boolean true; otherwise sign the user out for that attempt.

Align the login UI flow with the updated approval gating behavior: treat the sign-in result as authoritative for showing the pending-approval message and ensure the exact message "Your account is pending admin approval." is shown when the approval gate fails.

requirements.summary: Remove/disable any email-based profile lookup and any cached approval logic so login approval is never determined by anything except the fresh server read of users/{uid}.
acceptanceCriteria: The login flow does not query Firestore by email (no where('email'...), no reads of users collection to match email) and only reads doc(db, 'users', uid).

Approval gating does not rely on any stored/cached value (e.g., localStorage/sessionStorage/React state/React Query cache) to determine approved during login; it always uses the fresh Firestore server read result for that attempt.

file_operations.description: Audit and refactor the login-related code paths to ensure there are no Firestore lookups by email and no reuse of prior approval state between login attempts. Keep the approval decision confined to the per-attempt server-forced read of users/{uid}.

requirements.summary: Update LIVE smoke test/deployment verification guidance to validate fresh server read behavior, users/{auth.uid} path usage only, no email lookups, and include expected console/log indicators for troubleshooting.
acceptanceCriteria: Smoke test documentation includes a step proving that an admin flipping approved in Firestore affects the very next login attempt without a hard refresh.
Smoke test documentation includes a step to confirm the document path is users/{auth.uid} and that no email-based lookups occur.

file_operations.description: Update the LIVE smoke test checklist to explicitly validate that each login attempt triggers a server-forced Firestore read of users/{auth.uid} (not a cache-eligible read), that flipping approved takes effect on the next login without hard refresh, and that there are no email-based lookups. Add the exact console/log strings to look for during troubleshooting.

Update post-deployment verification guidance to mirror the new login behavior checks: server-forced read every login, users/{auth.uid} only, no email lookup, no cached approval state, plus expected console/log indicators to confirm correct behavior.
